Los complejos no nacieron para resolver: The complex numbers were not born to solve $x^2+1=0$ — that was simply declared impossible — but out of cubic equations. In the sixteenth century, Cardano's formula for certain cubics forced you to pass through roots of negative numbers even when the three final solutions were real and obvious. They were impossible to ignore: they were needed as a route even though they did not appear at the destination. Descartes called them “imaginary” in scorn, and the name stuck. Today they are indispensable in electronics, quantum mechanics and signal processing.
Los números complejos son la herramienta: Complex numbers are the everyday tool of electrical engineering. An alternating current has an amplitude and a phase — two pieces of data — and putting them into a single complex number turns fiendish differential equations into simple sums and products. The electronics in your house is designed that way. And quantum mechanics does not merely use them: it is written in them, because the wave function is a complex number at every point.
